newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Southcorp seeks Asia packaging growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Southcorp seeks Asia packaging growth.

text.p: Southcorp Holdings Ltd would seek further investments to grow its packaging business in Asia, central to an offshore focus for each of its three key business areas in 1996/97, chief executive office Graham Kraehe said.
Kraehe told reporters after the company's annual meeting that each of the businesses - packaging, wine and appliances - had a clear strategy for continued profit growth.

In packaging, he said the focus would be on expansion into Asia particularly through PET, films and lamination, similar to the recent A$18 million investment in China's Dalian Crown Making steel and aluminium can manufacturer.
"What we are generally doing is investing in packaging to support customers of ours who have got operations in Asia, so it is a relatively low risk strategy," he said.
"You will see things of the nature of the Dalian steel can venture ... you will see more of those sorts of things, you will see things in films, laminations, you will see things in PET," he said.

Kraehe said that in appliances, the company would focus on consolidating the turnaround of the United States water heater business, developing markets for Chinese water heaters and other Asian export opportunities, and on innovation and efficiencies.
"For the next year or two the broad objective (in appliances) is we are going to be seeking to improve earnings off the existing investment base," he said.

Kraehe would not give any profit forecasts for its U.S. water heater business, but said the rest of the industry generally had profited about five percent on earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) to sales.
"We believe we can get to that level but we are not going to make a commitment about what time frame we are doing it in," he said.

He also would not comment on whether Southcorp was now holding talks in its plan to establish a major alliance in appliances, to reduce its exposure to another domestic market downturn, saying only it was a medium term strategy.

Similarly, he said Southcorp continued its search for a major international wine acquisition, to enhance its international presence and reduce its reliance on each Australian vintage, but was prepared to be patient.
Its vineyard expansion would continue, although not at the rate of the previous three years, with the focus on premium wines and, to a large extent, red grape varieties, he said.
Asked whether Southcorp's second half of 1996/97 was likely to be better than its first half, Kraehe said: "Not by as much as last year."
In 1995/96 ended June 30, Southcorp earned a net A$124.22 million following a first half net of A$53.09 million.
